Large Language Models (LLMs) are a type of artificial intelligence (AI) model designed to understand and generate human-like text. They are built using deep learning architectures, most notably the Transformer architecture, and are trained on vast quantities of text data from books, articles, websites, and other sources.

Key Characteristics:
- Size: LLMs are "large" because they have a massive number of parameters, often ranging from hundreds of millions to trillions. This size allows them to capture complex patterns in language.
- Text Generation: They can generate coherent and contextually relevant text, from writing essays and emails to creating code and poetry.
- Understanding: They can perform various natural language processing (NLP) tasks, such as translation, summarization, sentiment analysis, and question answering.
- Few-Shot Learning: Many modern LLMs can perform tasks they weren't explicitly trained on with just a few examples, a capability known as few-shot or zero-shot learning.

Examples of LLMs include models from the GPT (Generative Pre-trained Transformer) family, LaMDA, Llama, and Gemini. They are the core technology behind advanced conversational AI assistants and a wide range of other applications.
